# 1 Chronicles Chapter 2 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 370v–371v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1CH_002_page_001.jpg, 1CH_002_page_002.jpg, 1CH_002_page_003.jpg

---

**1** The sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, **2** Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.

**3** Judah's sons: Er, Onan, and Shelah — born to him by a Canaanite woman named Bath-shua. Er, Judah's firstborn, was so wicked in the LORD's eyes that the LORD took his life. **4** Judah's daughter-in-law Tamar bore him Perez and Zerah, giving Judah five sons in all.

**5** The sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul. **6** The sons of Zerah: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara — five altogether.

**7** The son of Carmi: Achar — "the Troubler" — the man who brought disaster on Israel by taking what was set apart for destruction.

**8** The son of Ethan: Azariah.

**9** Hezron's sons: Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chelubai.

**10** Ram was the father of Amminadab; Amminadab the father of Nahshon, who was a leader in Judah. **11** Nahshon was the father of Salma; Salma the father of Boaz. **12** Boaz was the father of Obed; Obed the father of Jesse.

**13** Jesse's sons: his firstborn Eliab, then Abinadab, Shimea, **14** Nethanel, Raddai, **15** Ozem, and David — seven sons. **16** Their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. Zeruiah's three sons: Abishai, Joab, and Asahel.

**17** Abigail was the mother of Amasa, whose father was Jether the Ishmaelite.

**18** Caleb son of Hezron had children by his wife Azubah and by Jerioth. Her sons: Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon. **19** After Azubah died, Caleb married Ephrathah, who gave him a son, Hur. **20** Hur was the father of Uri; Uri the father of Bezalel.

**21** Later, when Hezron was sixty years old, he married the daughter of Machir (the founder of Gilead) and she bore him Segub. **22** Segub was the father of Jair, who controlled twenty-three towns in Gilead.

**23** But Geshur and Aram seized Jair's settlements, including Kenath and its surrounding villages — sixty towns in all. All of these had belonged to the descendants of Machir, Gilead's founder.

**24** After Hezron's death in Caleb-ephrathah, his wife Abijah bore him Ashhur, who founded Tekoa.

**25** Jerahmeel, Hezron's firstborn, had sons: Ram (the firstborn), Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah. **26** Jerahmeel also had a second wife named Atarah, the mother of Onam. **27** Ram's sons: Maaz, Jamin, and Eker. **28** Onam's sons: Shammai and Jada. Shammai's sons: Nadab and Abishur. **29** Abishur's wife was Abihail; she bore him Ahban and Molid. **30** Nadab's sons: Seled and Appaim. Seled died childless. **31** Appaim's son: Ishi. Ishi's son: Sheshan. Sheshan's son: Ahlai.

**32** Jada's sons (Shammai's brother): Jether and Jonathan. Jether died childless. **33** Jonathan's sons: Peleth and Zaza. These were all descendants of Jerahmeel.

**34** Sheshan had no sons, only daughters. He had an Egyptian slave named Jarha. **35** Sheshan gave one of his daughters to Jarha in marriage, and she bore Attai. **36** Attai was the father of Nathan; Nathan of Zabad; **37** Zabad of Ephlal; Ephlal of Obed; **38** Obed of Jehu; Jehu of Azariah; **39** Azariah of Helez; Helez of Eleasah; **40** Eleasah of Sismai; Sismai of Shallum; **41** Shallum of Jekamiah; and Jekamiah of Elishama.

**42** Caleb (Jerahmeel's brother) had a firstborn son, Mesha, who founded Ziph; and his son Mareshah, who founded Hebron. **43** Hebron's sons: Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema. **44** Shema was the father of Raham, who founded Jorkeam. Rekem was the father of Shammai. **45** Shammai's son was Maon, who founded Beth-zur.

**46** Caleb's concubine Ephah bore Haran, Moza, and Gazez. Haran was also the father of Gazez. **47** Jahdai's sons: Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph. **48** Caleb's concubine Maacah bore Sheber and Tirhanah, **49** as well as Shaaph (who founded Madmannah) and Sheva (who founded Machbenah and Gibea). Caleb's daughter was Achsah.

**50** These were Caleb's descendants. The sons of Hur, Ephrathah's firstborn: Shobal (founder of Kiriath-jearim), **51** Salma (founder of Bethlehem), and Hareph (founder of Beth-gader). **52** Shobal also had other descendants, including Haroeh and half the Menuhoth clan. **53** The clans of Kiriath-jearim: the Ithrites, Puthites, Shumathites, and Mishraites. From these descended the people of Zorah and Eshtaol.

**54** The descendants of Salma: the people of Bethlehem, the Netophathites, Atroth-beth-joab, half the Manahathites, and the Zorites. **55** The scribal clans who lived at Jabez: the Tirathites, Shimeathites, and Sucathites. These were the Kenites who descended from Hammath, ancestor of the house of Rechab.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 3 — Tamar:** Her story (Genesis 38) is one of the most dramatic in the Bible, but the Chronicler reduces it to a single genealogical fact. Yet her inclusion is theologically significant — she is a non-Israelite woman in the direct line to David.

**Verse 7 — "The Troubler":** The Chronicler changes "Achan" to "Achar," making the name a pun on *okher* (one who troubles). The narrative of Joshua 7 becomes a single epithet.

**Verse 10-12 — The road to David:** This compact genealogy — Ram through Boaz to Jesse — is the spine of the book of Ruth. The Chronicler knows exactly where this line leads.

**Verse 34-41 — An Egyptian slave in Judah's family tree:** Ten generations are traced from Jarha the Egyptian slave through his marriage into the family of Sheshan. The Chronicler records this without embarrassment — ancestry matters, but ethnic boundaries are more porous than we might expect.

*— PNEUMA*
